messages.author: b82af643aafe86d2
messages.subject: stan_lm: regression against a constant?
parts:
I thought I read somewhere that stan_lm() uses the same formula interface as lm(), but this doesn't work:

stan_lm(mpg ~ 1, data = mtcars, chains=2,prior = R2(0.75))
Error in lsfit(x, y, w, has_intercept == 1L) : 
  'names' attribute [3] must be the same length as the vector [1]


Am I missing something?

If I drop the prior specification, it still fails.  If I change that to stan_glm and drop the prior specification, it works.

Bill

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: stan_lm: regression against a constant?
parts:
Hi Bill, you're right that it's the same formula interface as lm, but the exception is that stan_lm requires predictors (it's not set up to just estimate a mean). But we have an error message for that case that didn't seem to be triggered for you, so I will look into that and get it fixed. 

Jonah

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: stan_lm: regression against a constant?
parts:
Thanks bringing it to our attention. The novel regularizing prior that Ben worked out for stan_lm necessitates that the model not consist only of an intercept. But a linear model using stan_glm allows for more traditional and independent priors (e.g. normal, student t) and and so it can estimate the intercept-only model.

Jonah

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: stan_lm: regression against a constant?
parts: On Monday, February 1, 2016 at 9:41:57 PM UTC-5, Bill Harris wrote:

I thought I read somewhere that stan_lm() uses the same formula interface as lm(), but this doesn't work:

stan_lm(mpg ~ 1, data = mtcars, chains=2,prior = R2(0.75))
Error in lsfit(x, y, w, has_intercept == 1L) : 
  'names' attribute [3] must be the same length as the vector [1]

As Jonah mention, there was a bug that prevented it from getting to the error message that would have said constant-only models are not supported by stan_lm.

However, think about what this
stan_lm(y ~ 1, prior = R2(0.75))
ostensibly means: A model with a constant only is anticipated to have a R^2 of 0.75! Every constant-only model has an R^2 of 0, which is why you were supposed to get an error message to that effect.

Ben

messages.author: b82af643aafe86d2
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: stan_lm: regression against a constant?
parts:
Ben,

Yes, that idea was ringing in the back of my head as I typed the formula.  At that point, I was merely trying to make stan_lm happy;I was going to go back to see what prior options stan_lm offered later.  I agree that stan_lm should have returned an error message.  Without thinking too much, I just expected stan_lm to check the formula and other argument syntax at this point and catch implications of the prior in the sampling phase.  It's good that stan_lm can catch this sort of error before the sampling.

Thanks for the fix and the insights.

Bill
